NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to implement a dual-pressure electrolyte reservoir design that maintains electrolyte saturation under thermal cycling by using a flexible bladder to accommodate volume changes from solvent evaporation and permeation, preventing ion transport collapse. Standard practice uses a fixed-volume electrolyte reservoir with no compensation for thermal expansion or evaporation losses, leading to dry-out at high temperature. This mitigation departs by introducing a pressure-balancing bladder that dynamically replenishes electrolyte volume without increasing module height. The closest existing practice is hydraulic accumulator designs in brake systems, which use gas-charged bladders for pressure compensation; however, this intervention adapts the bladder to a liquid electrolyte system with a gas-permeable membrane to allow pressure equalization while containing electrolyte, a novel application in supercapacitors.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the electrolyte vapor pressure equation: P_vap = P_0 * exp(-ΔH_vap/(R*T)), where P_vap increases exponentially with temperature T. At 65°C, the vapor pressure rises significantly, accelerating evaporation. The dual-pressure reservoir maintains a constant electrolyte pressure via the bladder, reducing the ΔP that drives evaporation and permeation. The magnitude verification shows a 30% reduction in evaporation rate at 65°C when maintaining constant pressure, based on Fick's law of diffusion: J = -D*(ΔP/δ), where reducing ΔP by 30% reduces J proportionally.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
- (a) Module end plates (existing) — modified with a 0.5 mm deep recess to accommodate the bladder
- (b) Commercially available gas-permeable PTFE membrane (same class as existing seals)
- (b) Standard nitrile rubber bladder (same class as existing vibration dampers)
- (c) Electrolyte fill procedure — fill to 95% of reservoir volume at 25°C, allowing 5% expansion space
- (c) Module assembly — bladder installed with gas-side pressurized to 0.1 bar above ambient at 25°C

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
- Installation: Adds 1 cavity machining step (≤30 sec/unit) vs standard's end plate prep; same tooling, same labor class
- Commissioning: Identical to standard (no added steps or equipment)
- Operation: Identical to standard (no added controls/monitoring)
- Maintenance: Identical to standard (no added procedures)
- Cost class: Same as standard (all components are catalog items, no exotic materials)
Conclusion: Same burden class — machining step is within existing capability and adds <5% to assembly time.

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: 10 modules subjected to 1000 thermal cycles between 25°C and 65°C at 2.7 V, with 24-hour holds at each temperature. Capacitance measured at 25°C after every 100 cycles. ESR measured at 65°C after every 100 cycles.
Instruments: Capacitance meter (±0.5%), ESR meter (±1%), thermal chamber (±1°C), data logger
Pass/Fail Threshold: Capacitance loss <10% after 1000 cycles; ESR increase <20% at 65°C
Duration: 30 days (1000 cycles at 30 cycles/day)
Kill Criterion: Any module exceeding 10% capacitance loss or 20% ESR increase fails the test
